item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sun Sep 20 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. item.description: Rhonda Vincent with The Malpass Brothers Rhonda Vincent is a powerhouse performer whose fiery talent and unmistakable voice have made her one of the most celebrated artists in bluegrass music. Hailing from Greentop, Missouri, Rhonda’s musical roots run five generations deep. She began performing professionally at just five years old with her family’s band, The Sally Mountain Show, gaining early experience on stage, radio, and television. By her teens, she had mastered multiple instruments and developed the work ethic and passion that would define her career. Her journey took a pivotal turn when a chance performance led to an invitation from the Grand Ole Opry—an early sign of the remarkable path ahead. Rhonda went on to build an award-winning career, earning the title “New Queen of Bluegrass” and becoming known for her signature blend of traditional roots and contemporary energy. item.title: The Ephrata Fair — Tue Sep 22 — Downtown Ephrata
item.description:
The Ephrata Fair, known as the largest street fair in Pennsylvania, has been a cornerstone of local history for over a century. Spanning several blocks in downtown Ephrata, this late-September tradition masterfully balances modern thrills with agricultural roots. The Ephrata Farmers Day Association manages the event, placing a heavy emphasis on Pennsylvania’s top industry through livestock competitions and agricultural exhibits. While the Midway buzzes with rides, games, and iconic street food, the heart of the fair remains its commitment to community heritage. From the famous Wednesday night parade to the unique farm displays, it offers a memorable, high-energy experience for residents and visitors alike.

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Sep 22, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description: With Father David Peck and Professor Randall Zachman Entirely on Zoom Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Sep 24, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

This 1980’s style show with a cast of memorable characters will show you mystery, adventure and maybe even a little fright as you speed down the rails on an adventure to uncover the source of a 40-year-old curse. item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Sep 23, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
